1939–1945

Kabataş – where the gold tanker Eocene anchored

While the ship lay at anchor here, diplomats argued over whether Poland's gold should go into the Ottoman Bank or on through the Dardanelles – with Germany pressing Turkey hard.

Theme
1939–1945
District
Beyoğlu
Period
1939
Visiting
No longer exists

The story

For three September days in 1939 an ordinary oil tanker lay at anchor off Kabataş – and in her holds was the gold reserve of the Bank of Poland.

After the German invasion the gold was driven out of Warsaw and gathered at Śniatyn on the Romanian border. On 13 September Colonel Ignacy Matuszewski took command of the convoy, and on the 15th the train reached the Romanian port of Constanța. Waiting there was the British ship Eocene, provided under an agreement with London. She crossed the Black Sea to Istanbul.

How to visit

There is no ship to visit: the Eocene sank in 1942, far from here, off the coast of Egypt. All you can see is the water where she lay at anchor. Stand at the end of the quay by the Kabataş ferry pier, or on the promenade towards Dolmabahçe Palace, and look out over the Bosphorus: somewhere here the Eocene waited. On the far shore to the south-east lies the Kadıköy side with Haydarpaşa station, where the ship went next. To follow the gold, take a ferry to Kadıköy (from Kabataş or nearby Karaköy – check the timetable). The waterfront is public.
